import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I’ll use the imagegen and Mermaid skills to create the infographic first, then validate a few diagram proposals. I’ll read the registered report through the SASE artifact workflow and check for output collisions before writing.


Both requested output names are available. The audited report read is still running; once it finishes, I’ll base the infographic and diagram candidates on that snapshot.


The report’s recommendation is to fix two existing completion defects, then add one shared controller for Markdown-writing fields. I’ll make the infographic an overview of that design, highlighting the Enter rule, trailing-text protection, and staged rollout.


The infographic is complete. I’m evaluating diagram candidates now. The strongest additions appear to be controller ownership and the link band’s lifecycle; the report’s tables already explain the key bindings, scope, and rollout clearly.


Two candidates passed: a view of shared-controller ownership and a state diagram showing acceptance, dismissal, and reopening. The pinned Mermaid CLI passed its smoke test with the guide’s browser workaround. I’m now checking both figures for readability and PDF fit.


The first renders exposed two issues: the ownership figure was too tall, and Mermaid misread punctuation in a state-transition label. I’ve shortened the labels and corrected the syntax. Both figures will need to pass another visual check and the 75% PDF-fit threshold.


Both revised figures passed visual review and the PDF-fit checks: ownership at 79.8% and lifecycle at 100%. Their anchors each match exactly one report line. I’ll now write and register the companion manifest for the linker.


The infographic and manifest are registered, and the linker status is `ready` with two proposals from 15 candidates. I’m using the SASE finalizer to declare the two new research files for the host’s commit.
